Comparison of definitions of angular momentum at null infinity
Szymon Bagiński, Jacek Jezierski

Abstract
The supertranslation ambiguity of angular momentum at null infinity creates a technical difficulty in choosing the proper definition for this conserved quantity. As a result, many different approaches are found in the literature. This article aims to review the most relevant of these notions and compare their most significant properties. A new definition of angular momentum at null infinity is also proposed, which is supertranslation invariant under certain assumptions.



Contents

1
Introduction

After the successful detection of gravitational waves by LIGO
[
1
]
, the topic of gravitational radiation became even more important in the theoretical understanding of general relativity. Currently, researchers usually describe radiating systems by analysing how different physical quantities behave asymptotically, which resembles how a given system is perceived by a distant observer. To make any valid conclusions, one needs to first define certain conserved quantities (e.g., energy, momentum, angular momentum) in a meaningful way, and then find expressions for their fluxes at the so-called null infinity. Although the matter is resolved in the case of energy and momentum
[
9
]
, there are still some major technical difficulties regarding angular momentum.

The problem arises in how the radiation zone is modelled mathematically - it is usually taken to be the boundary, called the null infinity, of a conformal completion of a given spacetime. Although conformal completions are constructed in such a way that they should resemble Minkowski spacetime at large distances, the group of symmetries of the resulting null infinity is significantly larger than the Poincaré group. In fact, it is an infinite-dimensional group called the Bondi-Metzner-Sachs (BMS) group. The BMS group consists not only of translations and rotations but also contains the so-called supertranslations
[
10
]
. The presence of such a kind of transformations makes defining conserved quantities, which, given Noether’s theorem, have to be associated with certain symmetries of a physical system, fundamentally difficult. As a result, one encounters a supertranslation ambiguity when trying to define angular momentum at null infinity. Hence, many different conventions may now be found in the literature.

The goal of this thesis is to review three different possible definitions of angular momentum at null infinity and to compare their properties which may be of importance when dealing with physical systems. Firstly, essential definitions and theorems are reviewed. Then, the concerned definitions are presented and analysed in how they differ from each other. Next, their fluxes and transformation rules under supertranslations are calculated. Finally, we present a new definition of angular momentum which, under a suitable assumption, is supertranslation invariant.

2
Background information

Here, we present the concepts of Bondi-Sachs coordinates and conformal completion. Moreover, we recall several useful facts from differential geometry on
S^{2}
.

2.1
Bondi-Sachs coordinates and null infinity

2.2
Supertranslations

As mentioned in Chapter
1
, the group of symmetries of
\mathscr{I}^{+}
is not the Poincaré group, as is the case in the Minkowski spacetime, but the BMS group, which extends the Poincaré group to include the so-called supertranslations.

Definition 2.3

(Supertranslation)
.

A supertranslation is a change of coordinates

(u,\mathchoice{x^{{{A}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.675pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{x^{{{A}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.675pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{x^{{{A}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.675pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{x^{{{A}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.675pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}})\mapsto(u-f(\mathchoice{x^{{{A}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.675pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{x^{{{A}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.675pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{x^{{{A}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.675pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{x^{{{A}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.675pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}),\mathchoice{x^{{{A}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.675pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{x^{{{A}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.675pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{x^{{{A}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.675pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{x^{{{A}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.675pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}})
, where
f:S^{2}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}
.

Also mentioned in Chapter
1
was how this fact gives rise to the supertranslation ambiguity of angular momentum. Hence, when comparing different definitions of angular momentum, we would like to know how they are transformed under supertranslations. In order to calculate that, we will need the following theorem.

Theorem 2.3
.

For any function
f:S^{2}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}
, the data on
\mathscr{I}^{+}
obey the following transformation rules under the supertranslation
u\mapsto u-f(\mathchoice{x^{{{A}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.675pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{x^{{{A}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.675pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{x^{{{A}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.675pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{x^{{{A}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.675pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}})
,

2.6
Integral formulae

Lemma 2.4
.

Let
\mathchoice{X^{{{A}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.675pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{X^{{{A}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.675pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{X^{{{A}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.675pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{X^{{{A}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.675pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}
be any vector field on
S^{2}
. Then:

\int_{S^{2}}\mathchoice{X^{{{A}\mathchoice{\makebox[12.5849pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[12.5849pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[6.39723pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[4.56943pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.675pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}{||A}}}}{X^{{{A}\mathchoice{\makebox[12.5849pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[12.5849pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[6.39723pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[4.56943pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.675pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}{||A}}}}{X^{{{A}\mathchoice{\makebox[12.5849pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[12.5849pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[6.39723pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[4.56943pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.675pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}{||A}}}}{X^{{{A}\mathchoice{\makebox[12.5849pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[12.5849pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[6.39723pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[4.56943pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.675pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}{||A}}}}=0.

Proof.

This follows directly from Stokes’ theorem written out in index notation (see
[
2
, Appendix E]
for details):

\int_{S^{2}}\mathchoice{X^{{{A}\mathchoice{\makebox[12.5849pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[12.5849pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[6.39723pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[4.56943pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.675pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}{||A}}}}{X^{{{A}\mathchoice{\makebox[12.5849pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[12.5849pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[6.39723pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[4.56943pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.675pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}{||A}}}}{X^{{{A}\mathchoice{\makebox[12.5849pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[12.5849pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[6.39723pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[4.56943pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.675pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}{||A}}}}{X^{{{A}\mathchoice{\makebox[12.5849pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[12.5849pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[6.39723pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[4.56943pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.675pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}{||A}}}}=\int_{\partial S^{2}}n_{A}X^{A},

where
n^{A}
is the unit normal to the boundary, and the integral on the right-hand side is taken with respect to the corresponding volume form on the boundary. Since
\partial S^{2}=\emptyset
, the integral is zero.
∎

Note that Lemma
2.5
can be easily generalised to products of multiple components of tensors of suitable types, which will be frequently used throughout this paper.

Lemma 2.6
.

Let
u,v:S^{2}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}
such that
D^{2}u=-k(k+1)u
and
D^{2}v=-l(l+1)v
, and let
n
be as in Lemma
2.3
. Then, if
k\neq l
:

\int_{S^{2}}n\mathchoice{\epsilon^{{{A}{B}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.675pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[6.383pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.383pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.96252pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.83037pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{\epsilon^{{{A}{B}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.675pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[6.383pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.383pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.96252pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.83037pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{\epsilon^{{{A}{B}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.675pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[6.383pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.383pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.96252pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.83037pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{\epsilon^{{{A}{B}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.01392pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.675pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.625pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}\mathchoice{\makebox[6.383pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.383pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.96252pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.83037pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}\mathchoice{u^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[12.5849pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[12.5849pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[6.39723pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[4.56943pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{||A}}}}{u^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[12.5849pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[12.5849pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[6.39723pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[4.56943pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{||A}}}}{u^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[12.5849pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[12.5849pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[6.39723pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[4.56943pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{||A}}}}{u^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[12.5849pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[12.5849pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[6.39723pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[4.56943pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{||A}}}}\mathchoice{v^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[12.95398pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[12.95398pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[6.68475pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[4.7748pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{||B}}}}{v^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[12.95398pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[12.95398pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[6.68475pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[4.7748pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{||B}}}}{v^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[12.95398pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[12.95398pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[6.68475pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[4.7748pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{||B}}}}{v^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[12.95398pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[12.95398pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[6.68475pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[4.7748pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{{||B}}}}=0.

Proof.

By integrating by parts, one obtains:

\int_{S^{2}}n\epsilon^{AB}u_{||A}v_{||B}=-\int_{S^{2}}n_{||B}\epsilon^{AB}u_{||A}v.

The vector field
X^{A}=\epsilon^{AB}n_{||B}
corresponds to rotations. Since, the Laplace operator is rotationally invariant,
X^{A}
does not change its eigenspaces.
Thus,
X^{A}u_{||A}=\epsilon^{AB}n_{||B}u_{||A}
belongs to the same eigenspace as
u
. However, unless
k=l
,
u
and
v
belong to different eigenspaces that are orthogonal to each other. Therefore, the considered integral, being in fact the inner product on the space of functions on
S^{2}
, is zero.
∎

3
Angular momenta at null infinity

3.1
The definitions

Throughout this section,

Definition 3.1
.

We compare properties of three different notions of angular momentum, defined in terms of data on
\mathscr{I}^{+}
:

•

Chruściel-Jezierski-Kijowski
[
9
]
(or rather Dray-Streubel

∎

So far, no additional assumptions about the physical system have been made. However, in order to simplify the formulas and to draw any meaningful conclusions, we shall assume
b=0
when dealing with fluxes.

Theorem 3.4
.

If
b=0
in (
14
), then the angular momenta from Definition
3.1

3.3
Transformations under supertranslations

Here, we present how different definitions of angular momentum transform under supertranslations. Similarly to the previous section, an additional assumption has to be made in order to obtain sufficiently clean expressions for comparison.

3.5
Transformations with inclusion of the superenergy terms

So far, we have considered only transformations of the data on
\mathscr{I}^{+}
, which gave the transformation formulae for angular momenta presented above. However, one could as well consider how the rotational vector field itself is transformed under supertranslations, which introduces additional terms into the transformation rules. To see this, we first note:

Theorem 3.8
.

For any function
f:S^{2}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}
, a rotational vector field
X=X^{A}\partial_{x^{A}}
on
\mathscr{I}^{+}
obeys the following transformation rule under the supertranslation
\bar{u}=u-f(x^{A})
,
\bar{x}^{A}=x^{A}
:

\bar{X}=X^{A}\partial_{\bar{x}^{A}}-X(f)\partial_{\bar{u}}.

Proof.

This is easily proven by noticing that

\partial_{x^{A}}=\frac{\partial\bar{x}^{A}}{\partial x^{A}}\partial_{\bar{x}^{A}}+\frac{\partial\bar{u}}{\partial x^{A}}\partial_{\bar{u}}=\partial_{\bar{x}^{A}}-\frac{\partial f}{\partial x^{A}}\partial_{\bar{u}},

and hence,

\bar{X}=X^{A}\partial_{\bar{x}^{A}}-X^{A}\frac{\partial f}{\partial x^{A}}\partial_{\bar{u}}=X^{A}\partial_{\bar{x}^{A}}-X(f)\partial_{\bar{u}}.

∎

In order to properly transform
J^{(\text{CJK})}
with the rotational vector field taken into consideration, we shall look back at the defining Hamiltonian. In practice, we transform the formula
[
9
, (C.100)]
by applying Theorem
2.3
and Theorem
3.8
. As a result, we get:

4
Conclusion

This article aimed to present different notions of angular momentum at null infinity found in the literature and compare their selected properties. To aid this goal, essential definitions and theorems were first reviewed. Then, the chosen angular momenta were presented, in two different forms. Consequently, the formulas for fluxes and transformations under supertranslations of those momenta were calculated and compared. Finally, given the computed transformation rules, new definitions of angular momentum were proposed, and their core properties were presented for comparison with other definitions.

Ultimately, it is worth noting that the proposed definitions of angular momentum, like
J^{(\text{CWY})}
, are described in terms of the potential
c
. However, one may modify these definitions in such a way to emphasise its geometric meaning. Namely,
c_{||A}
may be replaced by
{v_{A}=c_{||A}+\epsilon_{AB}b^{||B}}
, a first order potential for
\chi
, meaning that
{\chi_{AB}=v_{A||B}+v_{B||A}-h_{AB}\mathchoice{v^{{{C}\mathchoice{\makebox[12.79697pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[12.79697pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[6.57483pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[4.69629pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[6.22598pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.22598pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.8526pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.75186pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}{||C}}}}{v^{{{C}\mathchoice{\makebox[12.79697pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[12.79697pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[6.57483pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[4.69629pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[6.22598pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.22598pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.8526pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.75186pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}{||C}}}}{v^{{{C}\mathchoice{\makebox[12.79697pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[12.79697pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[6.57483pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[4.69629pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[6.22598pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.22598pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.8526pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.75186pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}{||C}}}}{v^{{{C}\mathchoice{\makebox[12.79697pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[12.79697pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[6.57483pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[4.69629pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[6.22598pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[6.22598pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[3.8526pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[2.75186pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}{||C}}}}}

\begin{split}&=\int_{S^{2}}\left(-\frac{1}{2}nD^{2}bD^{2}c+\frac{1}{4}n_{||A}D^{2}b(D^{2}c)^{||A}+\frac{1}{2}nD^{2}bD^{2}c-\frac{1}{2}n_{||B}D^{2}b(D^{2}c)^{||B}-\frac{1}{2}n_{||B}c^{||B}D^{2}b\right.\\
&\phantom{=}\ \left.-\frac{1}{2}nb_{||A}c^{||A}+\frac{1}{2}n_{||A}b^{||AB}c_{||B}+nb^{||A}c_{||A}-n_{||B}c^{||B}D^{2}b-\frac{1}{2}nD^{2}bD^{2}c+\frac{1}{2}n_{||B}(D^{2}b)^{||B}D^{2}c\right.\\
&\phantom{=}\ \left.+\frac{1}{2}n_{||B}b^{||B}D^{2}c-ncD^{2}b+n_{||B}c(D^{2}b)^{||B}+n_{||B}cb^{||B}+\frac{1}{4}n_{||A}D^{2}b(D^{2}c)^{||A}+\frac{1}{2}n_{||A}c^{||A}D^{2}b\right)\\
&=\int_{S^{2}}\left(-\frac{1}{2}nD^{2}bD^{2}c-n_{||A}c^{||A}D^{2}b+\frac{1}{2}n_{||A}b^{||A}c+\frac{1}{2}ncD^{2}b+\frac{1}{2}nb^{||A}c_{||A}-\frac{1}{2}n_{||A}b^{||A}D^{2}c\right.\\
&\phantom{=}\ \left.+nb^{||A}c_{||A}+nD^{2}bD^{2}c-\frac{1}{2}n_{||A}D^{2}b(D^{2}c)^{||A}+\frac{1}{2}n_{||A}b^{||A}D^{2}c-ncD^{2}b+2ncD^{2}b\right.\\
&\phantom{=}\ \left.-n_{||A}c^{||A}D^{2}b+n_{||A}b^{||A}c\right)\\
&=\int_{S^{2}}\left(-2n_{||A}c^{||A}D^{2}b+\frac{1}{2}nD^{2}bD^{2}c-\frac{1}{2}n_{||A}D^{2}b(D^{2}c)^{||A}+\frac{3}{2}n_{||A}b^{||A}c+\frac{3}{2}ncD^{2}b\right.\\
&\phantom{=}\ \left.\frac{3}{2}nb^{||A}c_{||A}\right)\\
&=\int_{S^{2}}\left(-2n_{||A}c^{||A}D^{2}b+\frac{1}{2}nD^{2}bD^{2}c-\frac{1}{2}n_{||A}D^{2}b(D^{2}c)^{||A}+\frac{3}{2}n_{||A}b^{||A}c+\frac{3}{2}ncD^{2}b\right.\\
&\phantom{=}\ \left.-\frac{3}{2}n_{||A}b^{||A}c-\frac{3}{2}ncD^{2}b\right)\\
&=\int_{S^{2}}\left(-2n_{||A}c^{||A}D^{2}b+\frac{1}{2}nD^{2}bD^{2}c-\frac{1}{2}n_{||A}D^{2}b(D^{2}c)^{||A}\right)\end{split}

By multiplying the above term respectively by
\frac{3}{2}
(or
\frac{1}{2}
) and adding it to
\dot{J}^{(\text{CJK})}
, one also obtains the flux of the proposed angular momentum
\dot{J}
(or
\dot{\tilde{J}}
).

Appendix C
Transformations under supertranslations

First, let us notice that, in view of (
14
) and (
4
),
b\mapsto b
and
c\mapsto c-f
under any supertranslation
u\mapsto u-f
. Therefore, to prove Theorem
3.5
, it suffices to substitute these into the formulae from Lemma

&\phantom{=}\ \left.-\frac{1}{2}nD^{2}bD^{2}f+\frac{1}{2}n_{||A}D^{2}b(D^{2}f)^{||A}\right)\\
&=J^{(\text{CJK})}+\frac{1}{8\pi}\int_{S^{2}}\left(3\epsilon^{AD}n_{||D}mf_{||A}-\frac{3}{4}n_{||A}f_{||B}b^{||AB}-\frac{3}{4}n_{||A}f^{||A}D^{2}D^{2}b\right.\\
&\phantom{=}\ \left.+\frac{5}{4}n_{||A}f^{||A}D^{2}b+\frac{3}{4}n^{||B}f_{||A}\mathchoice{b^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[12.95398pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[12.95398pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[6.68475pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[4.7748pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}{||A}}}_{{{||B}\mathchoice{\makebox[12.5849pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[12.5849pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[6.39723pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[4.56943pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{b^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[12.95398pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[12.95398pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[6.68475pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[4.7748pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}{||A}}}_{{{||B}\mathchoice{\makebox[12.5849pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[12.5849pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[6.39723pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[4.56943pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{b^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[12.95398pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[12.95398pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[6.68475pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[4.7748pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}{||A}}}_{{{||B}\mathchoice{\makebox[12.5849pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[12.5849pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[6.39723pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[4.56943pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}{b^{{\mathchoice{\makebox[12.95398pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[12.95398pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[6.68475pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[4.7748pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}{||A}}}_{{{||B}\mathchoice{\makebox[12.5849pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[12.5849pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[6.39723pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[4.56943pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}}-\frac{3}{4}n^{||B}f_{||B}D^{2}b-\frac{1}{2}nD^{2}bD^{2}f+\frac{1}{2}n_{||A}D^{2}b(D^{2}f)^{||A}\right)\\
&=J^{(\text{CJK})}+\frac{1}{8\pi}\int_{S^{2}}\left(3\epsilon^{AD}n_{||D}mf_{||A}-\frac{3}{4}n_{||A}f^{||A}D^{2}D^{2}b+\frac{1}{2}n_{||A}f^{||A}D^{2}b-\frac{1}{2}nD^{2}bD^{2}f\right.\\
&\phantom{=}\ \left.+\frac{1}{2}n_{||A}D^{2}b(D^{2}f)^{||A}\right)\\
&=J^{(\text{CJK})}+\frac{1}{8\pi}\int_{S^{2}}\left(-3\epsilon^{AD}n_{||D}m_{||A}f-\frac{3}{2}nfD^{2}D^{2}b+\frac{3}{4}n_{||A}fD^{A}D^{2}D^{2}b+nfD^{2}b\right.\\

&=J^{(\text{CJK})}+\frac{1}{8\pi}\int_{S^{2}}\left(-3\epsilon^{AD}n_{||D}m_{||A}f-\frac{3}{2}nfD^{2}D^{2}b+\frac{3}{4}n_{||A}fD^{A}D^{2}D^{2}b+nfD^{2}b\right.\\
&\phantom{=}\ \left.-\frac{1}{2}n_{||A}fD^{A}D^{2}b-\frac{1}{2}n_{||A}D^{2}bf^{||A}-\frac{1}{2}n(D^{2}b){||A}f^{||A}-\frac{1}{2}nf_{||A}D^{A}D^{2}b\right.\\
&\phantom{=}\ \left.+\frac{1}{2}n_{||A}\mathchoice{(D^{2}b)^{{{||A}\mathchoice{\makebox[12.95398pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[12.95398pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[6.68475pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[4.7748pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[12.5849pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[12.5849pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[6.39723pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[4.56943pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}{||B}}}}{(D^{2}b)^{{{||A}\mathchoice{\makebox[12.95398pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[12.95398pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[6.68475pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[4.7748pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[12.5849pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[12.5849pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[6.39723pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[4.56943pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}{||B}}}}{(D^{2}b)^{{{||A}\mathchoice{\makebox[12.95398pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[12.95398pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[6.68475pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[4.7748pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[12.5849pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[12.5849pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[6.39723pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[4.56943pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}{||B}}}}{(D^{2}b)^{{{||A}\mathchoice{\makebox[12.95398pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[12.95398pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[6.68475pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[4.7748pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}}}_{{\mathchoice{\makebox[12.5849pt][c]{$\displaystyle$}}{\makebox[12.5849pt][c]{$\textstyle$}}{\makebox[6.39723pt][c]{$\scriptstyle$}}{\makebox[4.56943pt][c]{$\scriptscriptstyle$}}{||B}}}}f^{||B}\right)\\

&\phantom{=}\ \left.+\frac{1}{2}n_{||A}fD^{A}D^{2}b+\frac{1}{2}nfD^{2}D^{2}b+\frac{1}{2}nfD^{2}D^{2}b-\frac{1}{2}n_{||A}fD^{A}D^{2}D^{2}b-\frac{1}{2}n_{||A}fD^{A}D^{2}b\right)\\
&=J^{(\text{CJK})}+\frac{1}{8\pi}\int_{S^{2}}f\left(-3\epsilon^{AD}n_{||D}m_{||A}+\frac{1}{4}n_{||A}D^{A}D^{2}D^{2}b+\frac{1}{2}n_{||A}D^{A}D^{2}b\right)\\
&=J^{(\text{CJK})}+\frac{1}{8\pi}\int_{S^{2}}f\left(-3\epsilon^{AD}n_{||D}m_{||A}+\frac{1}{4}n_{||A}D^{A}D^{2}(D^{2}+2)b\right)\end{split}
